name: Question 8
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3x-{y}^{2},\,y(0)=1
$$

Use the implicit Euler method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(0.4).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(0.4)≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=0.4,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=0.4-0=0.4.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the implicit Euler method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(3({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{new}})^{2})\cdot 0.4 \\  & =1.2({x}_{\text{new}})-0.4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+1.2({x}_{\text{new}})-0.4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
0.4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-1.2({x}_{\text{new}})=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.4$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-1.2({x}_{\text{new}}).
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+0.4=0.4.$ Then, the function $g$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =0.4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-1-1.2(0.4) \\  & =0.4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-1.48.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=1$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method. 

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=0.8({y}_{\text{new}})+1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{0.4(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{2}+({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-1.48}{0.8(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})+1}
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(0)=1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =1 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & =1.044444 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈1.044014 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈1.044014\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(0.4)≈1.04,$ rounded to two decimal places.

Since we want to find the value of y at x=0.4, we will use a step size of Δx=0.4−0=0.4.

Now, let's proceed with the implicit Euler method. In general, Δy is given by

Δy=ynew′⋅Δx=(3(xnew)−(ynew)2)⋅0.4=1.2(xnew)−0.4(ynew)2.

We substitute this into ynew=y+Δy and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as g(ynew):

ynew=y+Δyynew=y+1.2(xnew)−0.4(ynew)2 which gives the equation 0.4(ynew)2+ynew−y−1.2(xnew)=0.

So, the general form of the function g for step size Δx=0.4 is

g(ynew)=0.4(ynew)2+ynew−y−1.2(xnew).

Now, in the first step, the new x value is xnew=x+Δx=0+0.4=0.4. Then, the function g is

g(ynew)=0.4(ynew)2+ynew−1−1.2(0.4)=0.4(ynew)2+ynew−1.48.

We use a root-finding method with starting point y=1 to solve g(ynew)=0. We'll use Newton's method.

(ynew)n+1=(ynew)n−g(ynew)g′(ynew)

Note that the derivative of g is g′(ynew)=0.8(ynew)+1. Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

(ynew)n+1=(ynew)n−0.4((ynew)n)2+(ynew)n−1.480.8((ynew)n)+1

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with y(0)=1, we get the following:

(ynew)1=1(ynew)2=1.044444(ynew)3≈1.044014(ynew)4≈1.044014

Therefore, we conclude that y(0.4)≈1.04, rounded to two decimal places.
